footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. From pre-tax income to net income to common: after income tax and $21.1M of preferred dividends & other. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 12.1% to $717M in 2025. Net interest income rose 15.2% to $538M and noninterest income rose 3.8% to $179M; noninterest expense rose 3.0%, and the provision for credit losses was $11.5M, versus $11.2M.
Net income to common rose 34.6% to $185M, or $4.63 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 61.8% versus 67.3%. Bank of Hawaii returned $118M through dividends and buybacks.
highlights: Net income to common rose 34.6% to $185M.
watch: Net interest income depends on interest rates.
